questions.prompt: Assess this claim: Registered-user count alone determines GPU capacity.
questions.referenceAnswer:
Answer: False

Translate users into request rate, token rate and concurrency using workload assumptions. Gateways enforce authentication, tenant quotas and model routing. Queues absorb bursts but add waiting time; streaming reduces perceived delay without reducing total generation work. GPU scheduling must account for prefill and decoding workloads.

Semantic caches can return inappropriate answers if similarity ignores permissions or freshness. Rate limits and backpressure protect shared resources.

questions.prompt: An AI service meets average latency but violates its p95 target. What would you inspect first, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer: Inspect queue depth and stage-level latency percentiles. Load-test with realistic context and output lengths. Use admission control and capacity estimates tied to the target latency.
keyPoints: Inspect queue depth and stage-level latency percentiles.
Load-test with realistic context and output lengths.
Use admission control and capacity estimates tied to the target latency.

questions.prompt: How would you test that the change fixed this incident rather than hiding it?
questions.referenceAnswer: Keep a reproducible failing case for this incident. Use admission control and capacity estimates tied to the target latency. Compare the same workload before and after the change; record both the target metric and regressions.
keyPoints: Use admission control and capacity estimates tied to the target latency.
Compare the same workload before and after the change.
Check regressions as well as the target metric.

questions.prompt: The fix works in a small test but fails at production scale. What next?
questions.referenceAnswer: Inspect queue depth and stage-level latency percentiles. Measure representative workloads and separate resource, data and configuration differences. Stage a rollout with a rollback condition and rerun the original failure case.
keyPoints: Inspect queue depth and stage-level latency percentiles.
Measure a representative workload.
Stage rollout and define rollback criteria.

questions.prompt:
A support assistant must cite current policy, respond within a latency target and isolate tenant data. A fast uncited answer does not satisfy the task.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
A design starts with user tasks, quality thresholds, traffic assumptions and operational constraints. Separate functional requirements from latency, availability and cost targets so trade-offs can be evaluated explicitly.

Quality and operational requirements must both shape the architecture.
keyPoints: Quality and operational requirements must both shape the architecture.
A design starts with user tasks, quality thresholds, traffic assumptions and operational constraints.

questions.prompt:
Average retrieval is fast, but occasional retries consume the entire request deadline.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Allocate an end-to-end deadline across retrieval, model work and downstream tools. Tail latency matters because averages hide slow requests; component percentiles cannot simply be added to obtain an exact end-to-end percentile.

Measure end-to-end tails and bound stage deadlines.
keyPoints: Measure end-to-end tails and bound stage deadlines.
Allocate an end-to-end deadline across retrieval, model work and downstream tools.

questions.prompt:
A document analysis takes several minutes and repeatedly exceeds a short HTTP timeout.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Use synchronous responses for bounded interactive work and asynchronous jobs for long tasks with durable status. Provide request IDs and cancellation semantics so clients do not create duplicate jobs after timeouts.

Long-running work benefits from durable asynchronous status.
keyPoints: Long-running work benefits from durable asynchronous status.
Use synchronous responses for bounded interactive work and asynchronous jobs for long tasks with durable status.

questions.prompt:
Workers process 50 jobs per second while 80 arrive continuously. The backlog grows despite healthy workers.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Queues absorb bursts but do not create processing capacity. Bound queue size and waiting time, reject or defer excess work, and expose queue delay separately from execution time.

Sustained arrival rates above capacity require admission control or more capacity.
keyPoints: Sustained arrival rates above capacity require admission control or more capacity.
Queues absorb bursts but do not create processing capacity.

questions.prompt:
A policy changes at noon but the index still serves the morning version without indicating its age.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Separate ingestion, transformation and serving so failures can be replayed. Track source versions and indexing watermarks; retrieval should reveal when data is stale or incomplete.

Index freshness must be observable and tied to source versions.
keyPoints: Index freshness must be observable and tied to source versions.
Separate ingestion, transformation and serving so failures can be replayed.

questions.prompt:
Two tenants upload identically named documents and a shared cache returns one tenant's answer to the other.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Apply access constraints before returning evidence and enforce them consistently in search, caches and storage. Test cross-tenant queries even when identifiers or embeddings are similar.

Isolation must cover cached results as well as retrieval.
keyPoints: Isolation must cover cached results as well as retrieval.
Apply access constraints before returning evidence and enforce them consistently in search, caches and storage.

questions.prompt:
Three layers each attempt a request three times, potentially producing 27 downstream attempts.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Propagate a total deadline and limit retries across layers. Independent retry loops can multiply downstream requests and worsen an outage; reserve retries for recoverable failures.

Layered retries can amplify load multiplicatively.
keyPoints: Layered retries can amplify load multiplicatively.
Propagate a total deadline and limit retries across layers.

questions.prompt:
Bulk document jobs consume every worker and interactive requests stall.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Separate resource pools for workloads with different priorities and failure profiles. A circuit breaker limits calls to an unhealthy dependency; a bulkhead prevents one workload from exhausting all capacity.

Resource isolation prevents one workload from starving another.
keyPoints: Resource isolation prevents one workload from starving another.
Separate resource pools for workloads with different priorities and failure profiles.

questions.prompt:
All requests return HTTP 200 while citation accuracy drops after an index update.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Track latency, errors, saturation and task-quality signals separately. Operational health does not prove answer correctness; connect sampled quality reviews to model and data versions.

Transport success and answer quality are different signals.
keyPoints: Transport success and answer quality are different signals.
Track latency, errors, saturation and task-quality signals separately.

questions.prompt:
A rollout improves overall ratings but worsens answers in one language.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Offline fixtures enable reproducible comparisons; online experiments reveal real traffic behavior. Use guardrails and segmented analysis so a global average does not hide harm to a smaller user group.

Rollout decisions should inspect important traffic segments.
keyPoints: Rollout decisions should inspect important traffic segments.
Offline fixtures enable reproducible comparisons; online experiments reveal real traffic behavior.

questions.prompt:
A team chose a managed index for operational simplicity but later faces stricter locality requirements.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Record the requirement, chosen option, alternatives and conditions that would trigger reconsideration. Decisions should explain trade-offs rather than merely naming technologies.

Architecture decisions should document assumptions and trade-offs.
keyPoints: Architecture decisions should document assumptions and trade-offs.
Record the requirement, chosen option, alternatives and conditions that would trigger reconsideration.

questions.prompt:
A secure database is undermined by unrestricted request logs containing private documents.

What principle should guide the decision in this situation, and why?
questions.referenceAnswer:
Map data and authority across components and identify where trust changes. Review logs, caches and third-party processing as well as the primary database.

Security review must follow data through every derived artifact.
keyPoints: Security review must follow data through every derived artifact.
Map data and authority across components and identify where trust changes.
